decisions.reason: Broadening the permitted YouTube source collection does not change the requirement to select substantive moments containing a lesson, story, or real point.
The source decision changes which videos may be selected, not the requirement that each resulting clip contain a complete, independently understandable narrative.
Permitting any YouTube video does not alter the existing 70-to-85-second duration range.
The source collection was broadened, but the criterion to select moments with good hooks remains valid unchanged.
Video-source eligibility does not change the monthly approved-clip target, approval basis, or daily output expectation.

The current volume rule is tied specifically to Arden's voice, while the source decision permits any YouTube video. The evidence does not determine whether to generalize the rule to the selected video's primary voice, retain it only for Arden clips, or define another policy.

The source decision does not explicitly change the dedicated account's Arden branding, profile configuration, or audience-routing goal; altering those settings would require a separate client decision.
Allowing any YouTube source does not change the assigned batch count or the obligation to create and submit the launch production batch.
The clean, simple visual-editing standard and prohibition on heavy effects remain applicable regardless of the selected YouTube source.
The source decision does not alter the rule that B-roll must naturally support the message rather than serve as random filler.
Changing which YouTube videos may supply clip material does not remove or modify the requirement for client approval before publication.
The white-text-only and no-text-effects rules remain unchanged by the broader source-video permission.
